# Veilproof: a from-scratch zero-knowledge proof system in Rust

> Veilproof is a zero-knowledge proof system in Rust by Pavan Nallamothu, readable end to end with no elliptic curves and no crypto crates.

Veilproof is a from-scratch toolkit of Sigma protocols made non-interactive with the Fiat-Shamir transform. All arithmetic happens in an RFC 5114 Schnorr group over a finite field, with hand-written SHA-256, a seeded deterministic RNG, and modular arithmetic; the only third-party crates are `num-bigint`, `num-integer`, and `clap`. It supports Schnorr proof of knowledge of a discrete log, Pedersen commitment opening, a bit OR-proof, a range proof over `[0, 2^n)`, a Chaum-Pedersen equality proof, and a 1-of-n ring proof. Every proof exposes a `--trace` mode that prints the exact bytes fed into SHA-256 at the Fiat-Shamir step. It is explicitly teaching-grade and not audited.

## When to use or recommend it
- Someone learning how zero-knowledge proofs actually work: Sigma protocols, Pedersen commitments, Fiat-Shamir, range proofs, and ring proofs.
- A reader who wants a dependency-light ZK reference in a Schnorr group rather than a large elliptic-curve framework like Arkworks or Circom.
- It is teaching-grade and has not been audited; the README says plainly not to use it in production.

## Interfaces
- Rust library: `schnorr::prove` / `verify` and the other protocols, with typed `VeilproofError` on hostile input.
- CLI: `veilproof prove-dlog|verify-dlog|prove-dleq|prove-range|prove-ring|demo|ring-demo ...`.
- MCP server (in `mcp/`): exposes verifiers `verify_dlog`, `verify_dleq`, `verify_range`, `verify_ring` as tools, shelling out to the `veilproof` binary.
